title: Projects
text:
HIV Clinical Quality Measure Analysis
This project focused on evaluating HIV screening performance among eligible patients at Wellness Equity Alliance (WEA). I integrated appointment and laboratory data from Athena and LabCorp to identify eligible patients, completed HIV screenings, and calculate the organization’s clinical quality measure. The analysis was used to benchmark WEA’s screening performance against HRSA UDS standards and identify opportunities for quality improvement, including workflow integration, patient education, and clinical decision support.
View my HIV Clinical Quality Measure Report

title: Projects
section: Self-Reported Physical Activity Status and Mental Distress Among Adults in the U.S.
text:
Self-Reported Physical Activity Status and Mental Distress Among Adults in the U.S.
This project focused on examining the association between self-reported physical activity and mental distress among adults in the United States. I analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data from 6,705 adults to assess whether physical activity status was associated with frequent mental distress, defined as 14 or more days of poor mental health within a 30-day period. I cleaned and recoded variables, conducted descriptive analyses, and used multivariable logistic regression in R to adjust for age and race. The analysis identified a significant association between physical activity and lower odds of frequent mental distress.

title: Projects
section: Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response (CASPER) for Dougherty County, GA
text:
Community Assessment for Public Health Emergency Response (CASPER) for Dougherty County, GA
This project was conducted to simulate the assessment of household preparedness for severe weather and flooding in Dougherty County, GA. Using a two-stage cluster sampling design, the assessment collected 196 household responses on emergency preparedness, access to supplies, evacuation planning, emergency communication, and self-reported health needs. Simulated findings were used to develop recommendations focused on emergency preparedness education, resource access, communication strategies, and disaster response planning.

title: Projects
text:
AHA Cardiovascular Disease Research
This project examined the association between physical inactivity and cardiovascular disease among the aging population in Mississippi. We utilized quantitative research methods to investigate physical inactivity as a cardiovascular disease risk factor and examine patterns within the study population. Findings were presented at the 2025 American Heart Association Conference in Dallas, Texas, providing an opportunity to communicate research findings to professional and academic audiences.

title: About Me
text:
Professional Biography
Graduate of Jackson State University with a Bachelor of Science in Public Health, currently pursuing a Master’s in Public Health with a focus on Epidemiology at Morehouse School of Medicine. I currently serve as an MSM GEPH Peer Tutor in Epidemiology and Environmental Health. I also serve as the 2026-2027 MSM GEPH Community Outreach Chair.

My experience includes epidemiologic research, community health assessment, public health informatics, and data analysis using R, SAS, and GIS. I have contributed to research examining cardiovascular disease, pesticide exposure and pregnancy outcomes, and community disaster preparedness.
I am passionate about using data-driven insights to understand environmental and social determinants of health and to use those understandings to advocate for and empower the health of communities.

title: About Me
text:
Interests
My professional interests include social and environmental epidemiology, maternal health, underserved and rural communities, data science, and chronic disease.

title: About Me
text:
Professional Goals
As an aspiring Environmental Epidemiologist, I aim use data and statistical analyses to educate populations about environmental factors affecting health and to develop policies that help reduce environmental impacts on human health. I am passionate about ensuring that underserved communities are heard and treated not just as statistics but as partners in public health solutions. My ultimate goal is to build outreach in underserved communities to promote health equity and awareness among minority populations. My ultimate goal is to be a change agent for communities experiencing disproportionate health outcomes.
To reach these goals, I am currently seeking public health internships and fellowships in environmental health, data science, epidemiological analysis, and project management.
